why: Verse 1 means the territory of Benjamin where Anathoth lay, not the patriarch Benjamin.
Israel here is the nation and Kedar is the Arabian people or region (verse 10), not the patriarchs of those names.
Verse 16 names Memphis and Tahpanhes (Egyptian border cities); Bible Atlas links only Memphis here.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
Verse 15 means the town of Dan and the hill country of Ephraim, which are already linked as places, not the sons of Jacob.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
The people of Benjamin are the tribe living around Jerusalem, not the patriarch.
Verse 15 means the northern kingdom, called Ephraim after its leading tribe, not the individual.
Verse 16 means the northern town or territory of Dan, already linked as a place, not the patriarch.
Verse 26 lists Edom and Moab as nations, which are linked as places; the patriarchs are not meant.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
Bible Atlas puts Uphaz in India, but no one knows where this source of gold was, so the map shows no dot.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
Verse 26 means the territory of Benjamin, not the patriarch.
Verse 14 names only Lebanon's snow; Sirion (a name for Hermon) is not in the text, though some read the Hebrew that way.
The Benjamin Gate is a place in Jerusalem, already linked, not the patriarch.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
Edom and Moab here are nations, linked as places, not the patriarchs.
Bible Atlas draws Zimri on Susa's point, but where Zimri's kingdom lay is uncertain, so the map shows no dot.
Edom and Moab here are nations, linked as places, not the patriarchs.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
Ephraim and Israel mean the northern kingdom and the whole people. The Gareb of verse 39 is a hill near Jerusalem, not David's warrior of that name.
Bible Atlas puts the Kidron on the coastal plain near Ekron, but verse 40 means the Kidron Valley east of Jerusalem.
Judah, Israel and Benjamin here are the kingdom, the people and a territory, not the patriarchs.
Many Christians read the Branch of verse 15 as the Messiah, but the verse names only David's line; that reading belongs in the notes. Israel is the nation.
The Benjamin Gate is a place in Jerusalem, not the patriarch.
Judah is the kingdom and the Benjamin Gate is a place, not the patriarchs.
Edom and Moab here are nations, linked as places, not the patriarchs.
Israel here is the nation, not the patriarch.
Bible Atlas puts Lud at Lod in Israel, but verse 9 means a distant African people allied with Egypt. Its Carmel is the hill in Judah, but verse 18 means the headland by the sea.
Moab here is the nation, linked as a place, not the patriarch.
Bible Atlas puts this Bozrah in Syria's Hauran, far north of Moab; verse 24 names a town in Moab whose site is uncertain.
Gad is the tribe's territory, Esau stands for Edom and Kedar is a people, not the individuals.
Bible Atlas puts the Red Sea in its middle, but verse 21 means the Gulf of Aqaba at Edom's edge.
Israel and the hill country of Ephraim mean the people and a region, not the patriarchs.
Bible Atlas's Carmel is the hill in Judah, but verse 19 means Mount Carmel by the sea.
Israel is the nation and Ashkenaz is a kingdom (linked as a place), not the individuals.
